title: Be amazed at how Quraysh were kept safe together.
subtitle: The favour that followed the elephant
then: Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Zayd said this surah is tied to the one before: Allah stopped the elephant {reward}to unite the Quraysh and keep them safe in their city{/reward}. Ibn Jarir said the opening is one of amazement: {idea}be amazed at this favour{/idea}.
now: You have a home where you can sleep without fear and a city where you can walk to the shop. It feels normal. {idea}This surah says: be amazed.{/idea} Safety you never had to fight for is still a gift from someone.
old: The safety and comfort I have are just normal life.
new: My everyday safety is a favour from Allah, worth being amazed at.
try: Walk somewhere today and notice that you feel safe. Say alhamdulillah for it.

title: Winter caravans, summer caravans, always coming home safe.
subtitle: The trade that fed a whole city
then: Ibn Kathir says the Quraysh traded {idea}to Yemen in winter and to Ash-Sham in summer{/idea}. They came home safely because people {reward}respected them as residents of Allah's sanctuary{/reward}. Even those travelling with them were safe.
now: Your morning commute, the weekly delivery, the salary that lands every month. A rhythm so regular you forget it can break. {idea}This verse names that rhythm as a favour.{/idea} The regular things are the easiest to forget to thank for.
old: My income and routine come from my own hard work.
new: My work matters, but the safe rhythm that lets it pay off is from Allah.
try: On your next payday, give a small amount in charity as a thank you for the rhythm of provision.

title: So worship the Lord of this House.
subtitle: What gratitude looks like
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}directs them to be grateful for this magnificent favour{/idea}: single Him out for worship, just as He gave them a safe sanctuary. The House they lived around had a Lord, and {reward}He was the one keeping them{/reward}.
now: You thank your host after dinner. You thank the driver when you get out. The One who gave you the home, the food and the road gets {idea}a prayer squeezed in between other things{/idea}. Gratitude to Him has a shape: worship.
old: I am grateful in my heart. That is enough.
new: Real thanks to Allah takes the shape of worshipping Him alone.
try: Pray your next prayer as a thank-you for one specific gift, and name it in your heart.

title: He fed them when hungry, and calmed them when afraid.
subtitle: The two most basic needs
then: Ibn Kathir says whoever accepts this command, {reward}Allah gives him safety in this life and the Hereafter{/reward}. He cites the township that was secure and well-provided but {trap}denied Allah's favours, and tasted hunger and fear{/trap}.
now: A full fridge. A locked front door. The two things you would beg for most if you lost them. {reward}Allah gives them to you daily{/reward}, and asks only that you know who they are from and worship Him for it.
old: Food on the table and a safe home are just basics.
new: The basics are the biggest gifts. They come from the Lord who asks for my worship.
try: Before eating today, say: alhamdulillah who fed me. Before sleeping: alhamdulillah who kept me safe.
